data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous topicals & wound care_

**Class:** Recombinant growth factors for wound healing — becaplermin (PDGF-BB) gel 0.01%, epidermal growth factor (rhEGF)

## Mechanism of action
- Stimulate chemotaxis and proliferation of fibroblasts, endothelial cells and keratinocytes → granulation tissue and re-epithelialisation

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Diabetic neuropathic foot ulcers (becaplermin — approved), pressure ulcers, chronic non-healing wounds (rhEGF — available in India)

## Dose & formulations
- Becaplermin: amount calculated by ulcer size, once daily, covered with moist saline dressing; continue with offloading and debridement

## Adverse effects
- Local rash; possible increased cancer mortality with ≥3 tubes of becaplermin (boxed warning later removed)

## Contraindications
- Malignancy at the application site; infected or ischaemic wounds

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- PDGF-BB gel for diabetic foot ulcers — only with good wound care and offloading

_Sources: Khopkar ch.32 (Growth factor preparations); Wolverton 4e ch.54. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
